reading.body:
SIIA's AI lobbying is concentrated: 17 filings, one client, and a small core of lobbyists who appear on nearly all of them.

The pattern is a single-organization campaign rather than a broad industry push. Sara Kloek and Paul Lekas are each named on all 17 AI filings, Morten Skroejer on 16, Anton Van Seventer on 15, and Danny Bounds on 14. Below that core the counts drop sharply, to 10, 6, and then 2. The same client, the Software & Information Industry Association, appears on every filing, so this is one trade group's disclosure record and not a survey of who lobbies on AI.

The filings name 14 bills, all dated 2025 or later. That spread across many bills with a stable set of lobbyists is what sustained legislative attention looks like from the outside. For AI specifically, the bills are the point where compute and power questions become statutory text, and this data shows which proposals drew registered attention without showing what anyone argued about them.

What it does not tell the reader is position, outcome, or spending. A filing reports that a firm lobbied on an issue, not the side it took, and nothing here records whether any bill moved. The counts measure disclosure activity, not influence, and they cover one registrant only.

summary: SIIA filed 17 Lobbying Disclosure Act reports on AI held by this site. Its clients, the lobbyists named on those filings and the AI bills they name are below. LDA registrant id 48873.
